narrative_events.details: At Śaunaka’s twelve-year sacrifice the sages, having heard eighteen Purāṇas, ask Sūta for more. He selects Gaṇeśa Purāṇa among Upapurāṇas and says its teaching passed Brahmā→Vyāsa→Bhṛgu→Somakānta. Gaṇeśa is praised as Oṃ, cause of causes and ruler of creation, preservation, dissolution and cosmic operations; meritorious detached listeners desire hearing.
narrative_events.outcome: Sūta introduces the Somakānta account.

narrative_events.details: Somakānta rules Devanagara in Saurāṣṭra, learned in Veda and dharma, conqueror of kings, sacrificial donor. His retinue numbers10,000 elephants,20,000 horses,6,000 chariot fighters and uncounted infantry with fire-weapons, bows and double quivers. Ministers Rūpavān, Vidyādhīśa, Kṣemaṅkara, Jñānagamya and Subala serve and conquer territories. Sudharmā, his devoted charitable wife, bears Hemakaṇṭha, strong as10,000 elephants. Comparisons name Bṛhaspati, Dhanada, Earth, Ocean, Sun, Moon, Fire, Manobhava, Rati, Rambhā and Tilottamā.
narrative_events.outcome: Prosperous king and family established.

narrative_events.details: Prior karma brings Somakānta suppurating leprosy, bleeding, worms and wasting. He recalls protecting subjects, defeating foes with arrows and worshipping Sadāśiva, questions the karmic cause and rejects his present kingship and appearance. He proposes forest retirement and Hemakaṇṭha’s coronation, then collapses. Ministers and women revive him with wiping, fanning, medicines and mantra procedures.
narrative_events.outcome: King recovers consciousness and hears responses.

narrative_events.details: Ministers propose Hemakaṇṭha rule while they accompany the king. Sudharmā says she will serve her husband in the forest and asks ministers to stay with her son; individuals must bear their own past acts. Hemakaṇṭha refuses life, wealth and kingship without his father. Somakānta rejoices at their affection but defines filial duty as obedience, ancestral offerings and rescue of ancestors; he orders his son to rule with ministers and seek leave for the parents’ departure.
narrative_events.outcome: Somakānta insists on his son’s accession.

narrative_events.details: Father and son sit in the royal council chamber. Somakānta prescribes rising before dawn, remembering guru and chosen deity, asking Earth pardon for stepping on her, then morning hymns to Gaṇeśa, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Sun and Girijā. Hymns identify Gaṇeśa as giver of dharma, wealth, desire and liberation; Śiva as giver of boons to Nārāyaṇa and Indra, bearing trident, drum, serpents and tiger skin, destroyer of Manobhava and cities.
narrative_events.outcome: Morning worship instructions given.

narrative_events.details: Somakānta details earth selection and ritual cleanliness by class and life-stage, directional rules for excretion, repeated washing counts, tooth-cleaning with a tree-addressed request for strength, brilliance, cattle, intelligence, wealth and spiritual insight, then bathing, sandhyā, recitation, homa, study, libations, deity worship, vaiśvadeva, hospitality, meals with a Brahmin witness, Purāṇa hearing, giving and avoiding slander.
narrative_events.outcome: Daily purity and worship programme prescribed.

narrative_events.details: Advice turns to aid with property, life and speech, truthfulness, parents/gurus/cows, donations to vulnerable people, proportionate punishment after consulting śāstra or experts, distrust of proven enemies, sixfold policy, spies and messengers, restraint toward praise/blame, protection of returning suppliants, secrecy and conquest of six inner enemies. The king must preserve livelihoods, subjects, deities, groves and sacred sites, rescue Brahmins from debt and cows from mud, and respect servants, ministers, Brahmins and gods. Negative wording at25–27 and some policy phrases require collation; no definitive translation of those uncertain clauses is asserted.
narrative_events.outcome: Ethical and royal conduct taught, with textual uncertainties retained.

narrative_events.details: Somakānta summons Kṣemaṅkara, Rūpavān and Vidyādhīśa, priests, kings and queens, friends, guild leaders and citizens for Hemakaṇṭha’s consecration. Gaṇeśa and chosen deity are worshipped; maternal rites, auspicious ancestral rite, feeding and mantra-consecration follow. He entrusts his son to the three ministers and demands they obey the son as they obeyed him.
narrative_events.outcome: Hemakaṇṭha is consecrated and entrusted to ministers.

narrative_events.details: After coronation Somakānta distributes jewels, cattle, animals, textiles including Kashmir cloth, wealth and villages by rank. He leaves; people abandon work to follow. At a cool reservoir after two gavyūtis he asks pardon for government errors, loyalty to his son and leave to retire, attributing disease and separation to his own past karma.
narrative_events.outcome: King requests followers return.

narrative_events.details: Grieving citizens propose accompanying him to a few pilgrimage sites and returning after recovery. He refuses. Hemakaṇṭha again rejects separation; father insists his teaching must be obeyed, citing Jāmadagnya killing his mother on paternal command, Rāma’s forest exile with younger brother, and Lakṣmaṇa abandoning Sītā in the forest. He promises to return if fate restores fortune; son, three ministers and citizens finally salute, circumambulate and turn home with the army.
narrative_events.outcome: Hemakaṇṭha obeys and returns toward city.

narrative_events.cause: Son makes final appeal to mother.
narrative_events.details: Hemakaṇṭha asks his mother to secure permission for him to accompany and serve both parents. Sudharmā answers that the distressed king will not alter his decision and her duty binds her to her husband; she orders son home. He salutes, circumambulates, returns to the decorated capital, dismisses companions with gifts and governs according to his father’s instruction, balancing joy and sorrow.
narrative_events.outcome: New king begins dutiful rule.

narrative_events.details: Sūta resumes after sages ask about the forest. Somakānta travels with Sudharmā, Subala and Jñānagamya, sharing food and hardship. They reach a forest lake, drink, bathe, perform daily rites and eat fruits. King sleeps on sand while wife massages his feet and two ministers fetch roots, fruits and lotus stalks.
narrative_events.outcome: Retired party pauses at lake.

narrative_events.cause: Lake meeting creates opportunity for aid.
narrative_events.details: Sudharmā sees a radiant boy and asks his parents, name and origin. He identifies himself as obedient Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu and Pulomā, fetching water. He asks why the beautiful woman serves a diseased man and whether the disease was known before marriage. She describes her husband’s former rule, later karmic decline, minister companions, frightening forest beings and reversal from luxury to hardship, and begs Cyavana to become their saving boat.
narrative_events.outcome: Cyavana hears plea and identifies family.

narrative_events.details: Cyavana returns late with water, moved by the suffering. Bhṛgu asks why; son recounts the family’s plight, comparing the disease to Indra’s punishment by Gautama. Bhṛgu orders him to bring everyone. Ministers return with food just as Cyavana arrives with invitation. Sudharmā and companions follow him to the peaceful hermitage where natural enemies coexist and weather is mild and responsive to the sage’s will.
narrative_events.outcome: Bhṛgu invites the party into refuge.

narrative_events.details: Somakānta and companions bow to Bhṛgu. King praises the sage’s sight as purifying and explains that remedies fail despite dutiful worship; he seeks refuge and a remedy. Bhṛgu meditates, promises to explain prior-life sin and relieve distress, then provides oil massage, baths, six-taste food, adornment and soft bedding. They rest as if restored to royal comfort.
narrative_events.outcome: Bhṛgu reassures and hosts them.

narrative_events.details: Sages ask for the remedy and story continuation. Sūta warns that abandoning narration/hearing, mishandling a recited manuscript or withholding teacher-student exchange brings dumbness and deafness. Next morning Bhṛgu performs rites and begins the former-life account before the bathed king, wife and ministers.
narrative_events.outcome: Prior-life narration begins.

narrative_events.details: Bhṛgu says Somakānta was Kāmanda, late-born only son of wealthy Vaiśya Cidrūpa and charitable Sulocanā at Kolhāra near Vindhya. Parents doted on him and married him to devout Kuṭumbinī; seven sons and five daughters followed. Father died; mother burned with him and went to heaven. Kāmanda squandered inherited wealth with companions, rejected wife’s warning and sold the house; wife went with children to her father.
narrative_events.outcome: Family separates after squandered wealth.

narrative_events.details: Kāmanda becomes thief, adulterer, gambler, liar and violent oppressor. Citizens obtain royal leave to exile him. In forest he kills weak people and animals but flees stronger foes, gathers thieves and builds a large stone-and-wood house. His frightened father-in-law sends wife and children there; he lives amid family and robbers supported by killings.
narrative_events.outcome: Robber household established in forest.

narrative_events.details: Kāmanda seizes solitary learned Brahmin Guṇavardhana. Victim pleads he is innocent and newly remarried after his first wife’s death for lawful household and ancestral obligations. Saving life would make Kāmanda a father to him; even robbers protect suppliants. Killing would bring a thousand kalpas of hell, while relatives enjoying the loot would not share his sin.
narrative_events.outcome: Guṇavardhana appeals for life; no literal father-son kinship established.

narrative_events.details: Kāmanda rejects the appeal, calls it wasted instruction, refuses release and beheads Guṇavardhana with a sharp sword. Bhṛgu declines to count innumerable killings. Old age and illness bring rejection by household, descendants and friends. Through one trusted Brahmin he summons forest sages and offers gifts; they refuse a fallen donor, describing sinful association, then leave to bathe clothed and recite purifying verses.
narrative_events.outcome: Killing is followed in old age by rejection of his proposed gifts.

narrative_events.cause: Rejected gifts provoke remorse and temple restoration.
narrative_events.details: Illness, family neglect and Brahmin rejection lead Kāmanda to remorse. Brahmins identify an ancient Gaṇeśa image in a ruined forest shrine; he spends his wealth rebuilding a four-gated, four-towered decorated temple with groves and reservoirs; wife, sons, friends and kin take the remaining portion of wealth (hṛtam, not a gift). After death Yama’s messengers torture and bring him before Yama and Citragupta. Offered good or evil fruits first, he chooses merit and is reborn as Saurāṣṭra’s king Somakānta, rewarded for temple construction. Bhṛgu explains this by compassion for a suppliant and austerity power.
narrative_events.outcome: Merit-first choice explains royal birth; evil fruits remain.

narrative_events.details: Somakānta doubts Bhṛgu’s account. Multicoloured birds emerge from his body and tear flesh with beaks. He again surrenders, asks why violence occurs in the sage’s peaceful refuge and begs rescue. Bhṛgu identifies doubt as cause, promises that his huṃkāra will remove the birds, and utterance makes them vanish; king, wife and ministers rejoice.
narrative_events.outcome: Surrender and huṃkāra end bird attack.

narrative_events.cause: Sage prescribes hearing and consecrates cleansing water.
narrative_events.details: Bhṛgu prescribes Gaṇeśa Purāṇa hearing, recites108 names and consecrates water, sprinkling Somakānta. A small black-faced being exits king’s nostril and grows to seven palm-trees tall, breathing fire and foul blood/pus. It calls itself Pāpapuruṣa present in embodied beings, says mantra water expelled it and demands food and lodging, threatening to devour worlds and king. Bhṛgu orders it into a dry mango hollow to eat fallen leaves, threatening ashes for disobedience. Its touch burns the tree; fearing sage it dissolves into the ashes.
narrative_events.outcome: Embodied sin is expelled and confined in ashes.

narrative_events.cause: Tree-ash confinement requires accumulated hearing merit.
narrative_events.details: Bhṛgu directs daily deposition of Purāṇa-hearing merit in the tree’s ashes until mango regrows, when king will be sinless. King asks where text and reciter can be found. Sage names Brahmā→Vyāsa→himself transmission, offers recitation and commands bath and hearing resolve. Somakānta bathes at Bhṛgutīrtha; merely resolving to hear makes him disease-free, without blood, worms or wounds by sage’s grace. Seated with renewed radiance he requests the whole Purāṇa.
narrative_events.outcome: Physical disease resolves on vow; tree-regrowth and full hearing remain future.

narrative_events.details: Bhṛgu promises attentive hearing destroys seven births’ sins by Gaṇeśa’s grace, praises ineffable deity, reports Dakṣa heard from Mudgala after sacrifice destruction, restricts teaching to devoted Gaṇeśa worshippers and explains Vyāsa compiled eighteen Purāṇas and as many Upapurāṇas to preserve dharma in Kali.
narrative_events.outcome: Nested teaching is introduced; Somakānta continues listening.

narrative_events.cause: Vyāsa begins composition with pride and omits Gaṇeśa observance.
narrative_events.details: Bhṛgu narrates Vyāsa, son of Parāśara and a Nārāyaṇa portion, dividing the Veda and beginning Purāṇa composition proud of learning. Omitting opening Gaṇeśa praise/worship produces confusion and loss of recall in religious and ordinary affairs. He visits Brahmā in Satyaloka, honours gods and divine sages, receives a seat and asks why his knowledge has failed despite intended dharma instruction, seeking cause and remedy.
narrative_events.outcome: Confused composer seeks Brahmā’s diagnosis.

narrative_events.details: Brahmā advises considered action without pride/envy, citing Garuḍa’s reduced status as vehicle, an Ambikeya’s son losing everything through envy and Rāma’s destruction of kṣatriyas. He identifies omitted Gaṇeśa remembrance as cause: deity removes devotees’ obstacles and creates others’, governs Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Sun, Fire, Varuṇa and Indra. He orders surrender to elephant-faced deity, whose favour grants wishes; without favour even a thousand years will not suffice. Vyāsa asks deity’s identity, form, known manifestations, works and earlier worshippers.
narrative_events.outcome: Vyāsa requests fuller divine history; arc continues.

narrative_events.details: Brahmā distinguishes the single-syllable and six-syllable Gaṇeśa mantras among seven crore Āgama mantras. Devoted practice is said to yield liberation while living, mastery of siddhis, knowledge, free movement and forms. He teaches bathing, clean garments, cloth/skin/kuśa seat, purification, life installation, internal/external letter placements, breath control, mantra-sandhyā, whole-body deity visualization, mental offerings and recitation until Gaṇeśa appears ready to grant.
narrative_events.outcome: Practice method and prospective efficacy explained.

narrative_events.details: On an auspicious day Brahmā teaches Vyāsa the one-syllable mantra, advising him to ask arriving Gaṇeśa to dwell steadily in his heart; divine knowledge of past/present/future and successful composition are promised. Vyāsa says instruction dispelled confusion and resolves practice. Brahmā prescribes solitude and prohibits transmission to hostile/unfit recipients; improper disclosure condemns teacher and ten earlier/ten later generations. Devotional recitation promises offspring, wealth, pure knowledge, enjoyment and final release. Recipient-quality word niranukrośe at25 requires review.
narrative_events.outcome: Vyāsa resolves practice; actual divine boon to Vyāsa not yet narrated.

narrative_events.cause: Vyāsa asks for demonstrated mantra success.
narrative_events.details: Vyāsa calls Brahmā his guru and asks who previously obtained success by this mantra. Brahmā praises the eager disciple and explains Oṃ-seeded and Oṃ-framed mantras, universal Gaṇeśa worship and the need to remember him for unobstructed activity; he begins an ancient example.
narrative_events.outcome: Brahmā starts cosmic retrospective.

narrative_events.details: At dissolution winds destroy mountains, twelve suns dry waters, great fire burns and Saṃvartaka clouds flood. Gaṇeśa remains subtler than atoms; after long darkness the sounded single syllable reappears, becomes manifest Gajānana with māyā, and produces three qualities and Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Hara. The three seek their progenitor and instructions, searching21 heavens, space and lower worlds, then fasting and reciting for1,000 divine years without sight.
narrative_events.outcome: Cosmic triad continues seeking deity after unsuccessful austerity.

narrative_events.cause: Failed search and radiance overwhelm seekers.
narrative_events.details: The three search forests, waters and mountains, rest by a lake and encounter unbearable radiance. Exhausted and blinded, they withdraw through the sky, blame themselves and fear. Compassionately deity shows a pleasing four-armed elephant form with sword, shield, bow and śakti, single tusk, red dress and jewelled crown; Airāvata is named in comparison. They bow, touch his feet and begin praise.
narrative_events.outcome: Compassionate visible form permits praise.

narrative_events.details: Vyāsa asks how the three praised him. Divine glance grants clear understanding; their hymn praises transcendent Gaṇeśa, guṇa-linked Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Rudra forms, moon and power/world forms, and protection through feet-directed mind. Gaṇeśa names it Stotrarāja and promises pure devoted morning and three-sandhyā reciters sons, prosperity, wishes and final identity with supreme Brahman.
narrative_events.outcome: Hymn receives name and conditional efficacy.

narrative_events.cause: Triad requests devotion and divine task.
narrative_events.details: Offered a boon, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara request unwavering devotion and assignment of duties. Gaṇeśa affirms firm devotion and assigns creation to rajas-born Brahmā, protection to sattva-linked Viṣṇu and dissolution to tamas-born Hara; gifts include Veda/śāstra/Purāṇa and creation skill to Brahmā, free-form yogic capacity to Viṣṇu, one-/six-syllable mantras, Āgamas and destructive capacity to Hara. One knowledge-gift word26 is defective and remains unexpanded.
narrative_events.outcome: Devotion granted and differentiated capacities assigned.

narrative_events.details: Brahmā fears inability to create an unseen universe or obey correctly. Gaṇeśa gives divine sight and carries him inward by breath. He sees innumerable universes, each with its own divine and living worlds, including another Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, Prajāpati, Śaṅkara, Sun, Wind and Varuṇa. Unable to find limit or escape he praises and surrenders; deity releases him, and Hari/Hara are also brought out and rest. Precise nose/ear-route syntax45–46 is pending collation.
narrative_events.outcome: Vision overwhelms him; surrender gains release.

narrative_events.cause: Pride follows divine gifts and cosmic vision.
narrative_events.details: Somakānta asks how Brahmā created after cosmic vision. Bhṛgu explains Brahmā’s pride in knowledge and power: thousands of grotesque obstacles surround, strike, bind, mock, praise and manipulate him until he abandons pride and faints. Remembering Gaṇeśa he pleads for grace; heavenly voice orders austerity and the obstacles vanish.
narrative_events.outcome: Humbling obstacles end when voice orders penance.

narrative_events.details: Without mantra or location Brahmā wanders through water, steadily meditating on jewelled red elephant-faced deity with serpentine sacred cord, belly serpent and forehead moon. A second heavenly voice repeats the instruction to see a banyan, again puzzling him.
narrative_events.outcome: Banyan instruction prepares dream initiation.

narrative_events.details: In a dream Brahmā finds the surviving banyan amid dissolution waters. On a leaf appears four-armed, single-tusked elephant-faced child with crown, earrings and red dress. Child sprinkles him with trunk water, sits on his lap, rebukes his ignorance and teaches one-syllable mantra: ten lakh recitations by puraścaraṇa will bring personal appearance and creative power. Waking joyful, Brahmā bathes, stands one-footed on lotus, restrains food/senses and practices1,000 divine years; fire from his mouth afflicts beings and steadfast devotion moves Gaṇeśa to appear.
narrative_events.outcome: Mantra and long austerity yield deity’s appearance.

narrative_events.cause: Successful austerity precedes personal boon dialogue.
narrative_events.details: Radiant axe/lotus-bearing Gaṇeśa overwhelms Brahmā’s sight and memory. He reassures Brahmā he is the dream initiator, adopts gentle form and offers boon. Brahmā requests firm devotion, creation ability, removal of obstacles, completion of tasks when remembered, pure knowledge and final stable liberation. Deity affirms, commands manifold creation, says remembrance destroys obstacles and explicitly grants devotion and knowledge.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine affirmation enables fearless creation.

narrative_events.cause: Granted ability supports worship and creative duty.
narrative_events.details: For worship, Brahmā’s thought brings required articles through Gaṇeśa’s favour. At dakṣiṇā two adorned maidens appear, later named Siddhi and Buddhi; he offers them, performs lamp offering, flowers, thousand-name praise and circumambulation. Gaṇeśa accepts both and disappears; Brahmā resumes broad creation by grace. This passage does not explicitly call the maidens biological daughters or narrate a marriage.
narrative_events.outcome: Accepted offering and accomplished creation close penance episode.

narrative_events.details: Somakānta asks the next creation account. Brahmā produces seven mental sons and asks creation help; they choose austerity and reach supreme Brahman. A second seven also refuse creation despite knowledge; Sanaka and others are mentioned. Brahmā creates Brahmins and Fire from mouth, other classes from arms/thighs/feet, Moon from heart, Sun from eyes, Wind and life from ears, space from navel, heaven from head, Earth from feet and directions from ears, then waters, mountains and plants.
narrative_events.outcome: Creation established before new opponent episode.

narrative_events.cause: Ear-born opponents threaten their former boon giver.
narrative_events.details: Madhu and Kaiṭabha emerge from sleeping Viṣṇu’s ears, insult gods/sages/scripture and threaten to eat Brahmā, shaking Earth and Śeṣa with roars. Knowing through Gaṇeśa’s grace that Viṣṇu will kill them, Brahmā praises eye-resident sleep-goddess, addressed as Pārvatī and as creation/protection/dissolution power. He requests awakening, knowledge for Viṣṇu and delusion of opponents, explaining they worshipped him in previous birth and received various boons making them unkillable by him; his conciliatory praise failed.
narrative_events.outcome: Brahmā requests divine awakening and counterstrategy.

narrative_events.details: While Viṣṇu wakes opponents conquer heaven and Indra/Yama/Kubera residences; gods flee. Freed from Nidrā, Viṣṇu reassures gods, carries conch/discus/mace and blows Pāñcajanya. Afraid but eager to fight, opponents claim conquests of earth, lower worlds and21heavens and demand wrestling. Viṣṇu accepts, sets weapons aside and fights body-to-body for5,000 years without victory.
narrative_events.outcome: Long accepted wrestling fails to defeat opponents.

narrative_events.cause: Failed battle leads to changed form and music.
narrative_events.details: Viṣṇu takes a Gandharva form and plays vīṇā in forest, arresting listeners’ tasks. Hearing on Kailāsa, Śiva sends Nikumbha and Puṣpadanta to fetch musician; he honours him. Music pleases Śiva, Skanda, Gaṇeśvara, Pārvatī, gods and sages. Śiva embraces revealed Viṣṇu and offers wishes. Viṣṇu explains earwax-born foes, Brahmā’s appeal, awakening and failed wrestling, and asks a killing method.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva offers aid; Viṣṇu asks opponent counterstrategy.

narrative_events.cause: Śiva diagnoses failure as omitted worship.
narrative_events.details: Śiva says Viṣṇu entered battle without Vināyaka worship, losing strength. He orders worship: Gaṇeśa will delude foes and subject them, and by Śiva’s favour Viṣṇu will kill them. Asked the method, he distinguishes one-/six-syllable forms, chooses six-syllable after siddhāri-cakra and ṛṇa/dhana calculations, and promises success through observance. Exact technical calculation procedure is not given in these verses.
narrative_events.outcome: Six-syllable initiation sends Viṣṇu to practice.

narrative_events.details: Asked by Somakānta, Bhṛgu describes Viṣṇu’s six-syllable practice at future Siddhakṣetra: bāṇa-astra directional sealing, purification, life installation, internal/external letter placements, breathing, mudrās, mental and16offerings, then recitation. After100years Gaṇeśa appears and offers wishes, saying earlier worship would have assured victory. Viṣṇu praises cosmic deity and requests Madhu–Kaiṭabha’s death by himself, victory/fame over other foes and unfailing devotion. Deity affirms requests, strength, renown and freedom from obstacles, then vanishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Personal boon supports renewed battle.

narrative_events.cause: Received boon prompts installation and renewed challenge.
narrative_events.details: Viṣṇu builds a crystal temple with gold spire and four gates, installs Gaṇḍakī-stone image; gods/sages call it Siddhivināyaka and place Siddhakṣetra because he obtained success there. Returning to foes, he rejects their mocking diminishment with examples of small fire/lamp power; they attack his chest and wrestling resumes.
narrative_events.outcome: Renewed wrestling sets up conditional grant.

narrative_events.details: Viṣṇu praises opponents’ endurance and proposes giving a boon; māyā-deluded foes instead offer him boons, pleased with wrestling. He chooses that they become killable by him. Seeing water everywhere, they accept death from him, praise death with his remembrance as liberating and require a place not water-covered. He holds them on his thighs and cuts both heads with razor-edged discus; gods celebrate with flowers.
narrative_events.outcome: Conditional grant permits thigh-supported decapitation.

narrative_events.details: Gandharvas dance and apsarases sing. Viṣṇu reports to Brahmā his Śiva initiation, Gaṇeśa boon and resulting victory; gods/sages praise Gaṇeśa and the triad and return home. Regular hearing of this greatness is promised freedom from fear and fulfilment. Verse printed14 between40 and42 is treated as41 by sequence and colophon total45, with transcription variant exposed.
narrative_events.outcome: Celebration, report and return close opponent arc.

narrative_events.details: Vyāsa requests more after Siddhakṣetra. Brahmā narrates Bhīma of Vidarbha’s Kauṇḍinya, a powerful donor supported by tributary kings and vast army. His devout wife Cāruhāsinī is childless; he deems all fortune futile without a son, appoints learned ministers Manorañjana and Sumantu to keep kingdom for his return or divide it if he never returns, gives gifts and leaves with wife. At one gavyūti he sends citizens and unwilling ministers home, assuring their protection.
narrative_events.outcome: King entrusts kingdom and seeks aid.

narrative_events.cause: Seeking son brings couple to sage.
narrative_events.details: Bhīma and wife find lake and peaceful hermitage of Viśvāmitra with studying disciples. Sage promises a virtuous famous son and asks identity. Bhīma recounts failed austerities, giving and vows, trusts blessing, and asks prior fault/remedy. Viśvāmitra diagnoses proud abandonment of ancestral Gaṇeśa worship: deity’s anger prevents offspring. He begins why Gaṇeśa became their family deity.
narrative_events.outcome: Ancestral exemplum begins before remedy.

narrative_events.cause: Ancestral family context explains present Bhīma.
narrative_events.details: Viśvāmitra recalls ancestor Vallabha, described as seventh earlier person from Bhīma. After long delay a son is born mute, deaf, hunchbacked and suppurating. Mother Kamalā laments childlessness would be better and wishes death. Vallabha comforts her through karma and proposes gems, mantra, medicines, penance, recitation, deity worship and pilgrimage; she bathes child and celebrates birth with Brahmin gifts.
narrative_events.outcome: Ill child retained and remedies begin.

narrative_events.cause: Long failed remedies lead to exile.
narrative_events.details: Vallabha consults and rewards priests, names child Dakṣa and undertakes remedies and12years of austerity for his health and offspring prosperity. Failing, he angrily drives mother and son out. Kamalā carries child, begs village to village and is robbed of clothes/jewels. At another settlement she places him in Śiva shrine while begging; breeze from a devoted Brahmin’s body restores divine form, sight, hearing and speech through Lambodara’s favour. Mother rejoices; citizens feed and clothe them, and child asks mother family details before answering an inquirer.
narrative_events.outcome: Devotee-body breeze unexpectedly restores child.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa reports father Vallabha of Bhānunagara in Karṇāṭa and mother Kamalā; healing follows exile and bodily breeze. A compassionate Brahmin teaches both Gaṇeśa worship. Mother and son stand on one great toe, live on air, emaciate and recite eight-syllable deity-name/dative mantra framed by Oṃ. Gaṇeśa appears four-armed, single-tusked, with belly serpent, yellow silks and crown, then adopts Brahmin form and offers desired boon.
narrative_events.outcome: Deity personally appears and offers boon.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa praises elephant and Brahmin manifestations as supreme cause, witness, cosmic deities/elements, time, knowledge, social forms and emotions. Gaṇeśa says he is pleased and eager to give yet will not grant, lest his devotee be angry: Mudgala, whose bodily breeze healed Dakṣa, will give all wishes and appear when remembered. God vanishes; Dakṣa laments, falls and searches.
narrative_events.outcome: Boon deferred to Mudgala; seeker grieves.

narrative_events.details: Distraught Dakṣa questions travellers and trees about Gaṇeśa, collapses and dreams a Brahmin saying Mudgala has given what he earlier requested. A passing Brahmin directs him to Mudgala’s refuge hermitage; he finds learned radiant yogi worshipping four-armed, three-eyed Gaṇeśa image with16offerings, prostrates and is asked identity and suffering.
narrative_events.outcome: Dream and directions bring seeker to Mudgala.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa recounts Bhānunagara parentage, congenital disabilities, citizens’ rejection, father’s12year failure and expulsion, mother’s arrival at Kauṇḍinya and healing breeze from Mudgala. Comparing Ahalyā’s recovery by Raghunātha’s feet, he vows to preserve body only upon seeing healer. He says both practiced until Gaṇeśa appeared and Kamalā obtained desired wishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Healing and mother’s fulfilment recounted as Dakṣa’s speech.

narrative_events.cause: Dakṣa explains devotional vision and requested wishes.
narrative_events.details: Dakṣa recounts Brahmin manifestation, elephant form with axe, lotus, rosary and modakas, referral to Mudgala and disappearance. Remembering the offer after fainting, he says he asked enduring household wealth and firm devotion; heavenly voice answered given. He interprets Mudgala and Gaṇeśa as identical. This report differs in elaboration/order from chapter20, whose immediate boon refusal is retained separately.
narrative_events.outcome: Speech reports explicit wealth/devotion request and heavenly grant.

narrative_events.details: Mudgala praises Dakṣa’s devotion, saying his own1,000years’ austerity never produced such sight, and bows to the devotee. Both bow and embrace as guru-related friends. Mudgala teaches one-syllable mantra with recitation and meditation, orders daily practice and warns abandonment brings complete ruin; enduring devotion promises subjection of Indra’s guardians, enjoyment and final liberation.
narrative_events.outcome: Daily mantra practice with explicit abandonment consequence prescribed.

narrative_events.cause: Question about prior cause opens another past-life account.
narrative_events.details: Bhīma asks Viśvāmitra why healing and sight came to Dakṣa despite Mudgala’s long austerity, and who he was before. Sage narrates Vaiśya Kalyāṇa of Pallī in Sindhu, devout donor, and wife Indumatī, whose son Ballāla grows devoted. With other boys he bathes and installs a beautiful stone as Gaṇeśa, worships with dūrvā/leaves, meditation, name-recitation, song, dance, forest shelters, flowers, lamps and offerings, and recites Purāṇa/dharma teaching.
narrative_events.outcome: Children’s intense worship established.

narrative_events.details: Boys forget hunger/thirst; parents blame Ballāla for daily absence and wasting, threaten binding/beating and Kalyāṇa’s expulsion through town ruler. Angry father takes a large club, smashes worship shelter, scatters boys, beats unmoving Ballāla bloody, throws image away and binds son to tree with vine nooses. He taunts that god must feed/release him and threatens death if he returns home.
narrative_events.outcome: Devotee remains bound and injured after shrine destruction.

narrative_events.cause: Abuse evokes curse and complete surrender.
narrative_events.details: Ballāla laments apparent failure of obstacle-removing deity and invokes unchanging natural duties of Śeṣa, Sun, Moon and Fire. He curses shrine-destroying father to blindness, deafness, hunchback and muteness if his devotion is true, declares faith cannot be bound and surrenders life. Gaṇeśa appears as Brahmin; radiance loosens bonds and body becomes whole without wounds/blood, with pure knowledge.
narrative_events.outcome: Divine appearance releases and heals devotee.

narrative_events.cause: Restored devotee praises and requests continuing protection.
narrative_events.details: Ballāla praises deity as universal parent/cause; Gaṇeśa embraces him and confirms shrine destroyer’s hell and bodily curse including bleeding, followed by father expelling him with mother in next embodiment. Ballāla asks firm devotion and deity’s lasting protection at this site. Grant names Ballālavināyaka, affirms steadfast mind/devotion and promises wishes to Pallī pilgrims on Bhādrapada bright fourth. God vanishes; Ballāla installs image and builds temple with Brahmins. Hearing this account is said to remove sins and fulfil wishes.
narrative_events.outcome: Devotion, site manifestation and temple installation granted; family aftermath continues23.

narrative_events.details: Bhīma asks Kalyāṇa’s fate. Viśvāmitra says Ballāla’s curse immediately produces bleeding wounds, foulness, muteness, blindness and deafness in Kalyāṇa. Indumatī initially laments apparently blameless devout husband, then hears son’s binding and goes with townspeople. Seeing Ballāla whole and worshipping restored shrine, she rebukes misleading reports; astonished people acknowledge devotion and mother embraces son joyfully.
narrative_events.outcome: Mother sees healed son and temple.

narrative_events.cause: Mother appeals to competing filial duty.
narrative_events.details: Indumatī asks son home to cure suffering father, defending paternal discipline and filial obedience, feeding/protection and remedial medicines/mantra/prayer. Ballāla answers Gaṇeśa is universal mother/father, all kinship incidental and karmic fruits deserved; he surrendered life and received life/knowledge. Seeing fallen shrine-destroyer is harmful; mother should release attachment and serve husband. She begs curse relief through compassion.
narrative_events.outcome: Immediate healing refused; mother seeks relief terms.

narrative_events.cause: Mother begs relief rather than disputing curse.
narrative_events.details: Ballāla predicts Kalyāṇa becomes kṣatriya Vallabha, Indumatī becomes Kamalā and the afflicted man becomes her son Dakṣa. Vallabha’s12years fail; mother/son are exiled, then Gaṇeśa-devoted Brahmin touch heals son and deity vision grants divine form. This is named curse-relief cause; mother leaves with mixed sorrow/hope. Gaṇeśa’s divine vehicle takes Ballāla heavenward. Viśvāmitra confirms prediction occurred: she was born Kamalā, he a kṣatriya. Printed final45 versus total46 is retained as numbering uncertainty.
narrative_events.outcome: Future relief conditions and completed rebirth identified; Ballāla ascends.

narrative_events.details: Bhīma asks Dakṣa’s practice. At ruined forest Gaṇeśa shrine near Kauṇḍinya he practices Mudgala’s one-syllable mantra, worships and offers roots/fruit with imagined dakṣiṇā. Text says twelve years6, then21days8 before dawn dream: elephant garlands him, lifts him to shoulder and enters flagged city. Kamalā interprets elephant as Vināyaka and mount as kingship. Dakṣa promises her vehicle/villages/jewels and charitable rites if fulfilled; she wishes long life and steady reverence. Duration phrasing is preserved, not harmonized.
narrative_events.outcome: Dream predicts kingship; mother interprets and receives conditional promises.

narrative_events.details: At Kauṇḍinya King Candrasena dies through ripened karma and merits heaven by divine vehicle. Citizens and childless wife Sulabhā mourn, collapse and reproach separation. Ministers Sumantu and Manorañjana ask who will govern and propose following him. These ancient ministers are context-distinct from current Bhīma’s same-named ministers.
narrative_events.outcome: Court mourns with no heir.

narrative_events.cause: Funeral and continued vacancy require decision.
narrative_events.details: A learned Brahmin rebukes self-serving grief and orders funeral care by an adopted or other son; Sumantu performs rites, all give sesame water, then baths and household return follow. After13days they feed and honour queen. In succession uncertainty Mudgala arrives and prescribes royal elephant Gahana carrying lotus garland: whoever it garlands in assembly shall rule. All approve the sage’s supernormal insight.
narrative_events.outcome: Elephant-selection rule accepted.

narrative_events.details: At auspicious assembly queen gives garland to decorated Gahana. It passes city candidates, leaves town and garlands Dakṣa worshipping Gaṇeśa, fulfilling dream. People honour king with clothes/jewels; heavenly flowers and music celebrate. Dakṣa gives gifts, honours mother, places her in palanquin, rides elephant and enters decorated city with two mounted ministers.
narrative_events.outcome: Dakṣa chosen king and brings mother to capital.

narrative_events.cause: Kingship prompts gratitude and further blessing.
narrative_events.details: Dakṣa sends Sumantu with vehicle/royal insignia to invite Mudgala, meets him, bows and seats sage on his throne. Attributing health and kingship to sage and identifying him devotionally with Vināyaka, king asks hand on his head to enjoy all wishes long. Mudgala assures no enemy-caused fear and fulfilment of every desired wish. King rewards sage/Brahmins/ministers and enlarges old Gaṇeśa temple at Kuṇḍina.
narrative_events.outcome: Protective blessing and temple enlargement follow.

narrative_events.details: Vallabha arrives on hearing news. King Vīrasena, instructed by Gaṇeśa in dream, gives his marriage-seeking daughter to Dakṣa. Their son is Bṛhadbhānu; successive line is Khaḍgadhara→Sulabha→Padmākara→Vapurdīpta→Citraseṇa→current Bhīma. Hearing ancestral line, Bhīma asks Viśvāmitra when/how Vināyaka will favour him. Exact ancestor counting against19.40 remains a collation task.
narrative_events.outcome: Marriage and descendant genealogy close ancestral Dakṣa sequence; present Bhīma resumes.

narrative_events.details: Vyāsa asks Bhīma’s remedy. Viśvāmitra teaches one-syllable mantra and directs observance in Dakṣa’s temple, promising wishes, four aims and return home. Bhīma and Cāruhāsinī return honoured by citizens/ministers. King practices fasting, mantra and constant Gaṇeśa awareness in Dakṣa shrine; seeing god everywhere people think him possessed. Gaṇeśa takes his hand, calls him liberated and offers wish; king says he knows only divine feet. Deity promises virtuous golden-bodied son and commands deity/Brahmin worship. Shortly son is born and named Rukmāṅgada amid gifts.
narrative_events.outcome: Initiation and devotion yield promised son’s birth.

narrative_events.cause: Promised son grows and inherits worship.
narrative_events.details: Bhīma entrusts growing Rukmāṅgada to Kapila for education; son grasps teaching on hearing and becomes learned/strong, compared with Gajakarṇa. Father consecrates him and gives priestly gifts; son increases Gaṇeśa devotion and recites father-taught one-syllable mantra daily. Hunting one day he kills game, becomes exhausted and reaches a sage’s peaceful hermitage.
narrative_events.outcome: Education, accession and hunt open new opponent episode.
